findings.why_it_matters: The NOTE table's two-line column heading 'Argument-1 characteristics' is split: 'Argument-1' is detached as a stray paragraph above the table and the column header reads only 'characteristics'.

findings.pdf_says:
$**,**9.99              0
BINARY-CHAR SIGNED      -128 (assuming an 8-bit twos-complement representation)
BINARY-CHAR UNSIGNED    0 (assuming an 8-bit twos-compliment representation)
findings.markdown_says:
$\*\*,\*\*9.99 0\
BINARY-CHAR SIGNED -128 (assuming an 8-bit twos-complement representation)\
BINARY-CHAR UNSIGNED 0 (assuming an 8-bit twos-compliment representation)
findings.why_it_matters: These three rows continue the two-column 'Argument-1 characteristics / Value returned' table of the LOWEST-ALGEBRAIC NOTE from page 715, but the markdown renders them as run-together text lines outside any table, so the argument and value columns are merged (e.g. '$**,**9.99 0').
The subscripts that index the occurrences of argument-1 were flattened into the name, so the equivalent arithmetic expression for MEAN now reads as operands named argument-11 and argument-12.

findings.pdf_says: ((argument-1₁ + argument-1₂ +... + argument-1ₙ) / n)  [1, 2 and n printed as subscripts]
findings.why_it_matters: The subscripts 1, 2 and n were flattened into the operand names, so the general MEAN expression reads as argument-11, argument-12 and argument-1n instead of the 1st, 2nd and nth occurrences of argument-1.
